extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of literary criticism; literary scholars and critics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and critical criteria for evaluating poets, dramatists, and prose-writers (especially Shakespeare, Dante, Charles Lamb) focusing on qualities like 'vision', moral tone, universality, craft, and the relation of art to nature and society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeing / Vision as primary poetic faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poet's first gift is to 'See'—to discern the inner heart and harmony of things; 'The word that will describe the thing, follows of itself from such clear intense sight of the thing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the writer displays 'a calmly seeing eye' or 'a power of vision' that dissolves objects 'as in light' so the 'inward mechanism' is visible. A strong poet reveals 'the perfect structure' of things and can out of chaos create order ('Fiat lux').

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of faculties / indivisibility of intellect and imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculties (intellect, imagination, fancy, etc.) are not separable; they are different figures of the same power of insight; a writer's gifts are physiognomical of one unified inner force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess work for integrated capability — not isolated cleverness in one aspect but harmony among thought, feeling, fancy, and moral sense. Beware treating faculties as compartmentalized when judging a poet's capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral quality as prerequisite to true knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Without morality, intellect is impossible; 'To know a thing... a man must first love the thing, sympathise with it: that is, be virtuously related to it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the writer's moral sympathy and justice: does the author's temperament enable genuine understanding of subjects (nature, people)? A deficient moral relation produces mean, superficial knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrait-painting / fidelity in delineating character
rubrics_metrics.description: Greatness in 'delineating of men and things, especially of men' — characters are shown in their 'round completeness', with inward mechanism visible, like 'watches with dial-plates of transparent crystal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the author's ability to render rounded, convincing characters: do portrayals reveal both surface and inner life; are characters set forth with love and justice so they become 'complete' human presences?

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding materials and structural fitness
rubrics_metrics.description: The artist 'discerns, knows as by instinct, what condition he works under, what his materials are, what his own force and its relation to them is' — the built house seems fit because the maker understands materials and order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how well the creator chooses, shapes and orders material: is there a sense that 'like joins to like', method emerges from confusion, and the sequence and ending are 'fit' and appropriate to the subject?

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative unconscious growth (art as natural growth)
rubrics_metrics.description: The noblest worth of art is not artifice but growth 'from the deeps of Nature' — works that 'grow-up un_consciously, from the unknown deeps in him', with symmetry 'grounded on Nature's own laws.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for spontaneity and organic unity rather than over-engineered contrivance; value work that seems to arise naturally from the writer's deepest nature and resonates with universal truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality, sincerity and endurance
rubrics_metrics.description: A great writer reaches deep down 'to the universal and perennial' and is 'sincere' so that his voice can last like Homer or Aeschylus; universality binds readers across times and places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work speaks to perennial human experience and does so sincerely rather than by ephemeral topicality; universality is a marker of long-term cultural value and national/personal voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of mirth and pity; humour vs wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between 'wit' (transitory, 'crackling of thorns') and 'humour' (laughter that 'blends with tears' and is 'one with pity'); good laughter is sympathetic and ennobling, not at misery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating comic elements, prefer humour that arises from sympathy and enlarges human understanding; avoid mere cleverness that mocks weakness or is cheaply amusing without moral sympathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to concrete detail and the retrospective critic's role
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic/artist works 'close to the concrete, to the details, great or small' and often acts as a 'discoverer' or preserver of past excellence; 'in the making of prose he realises the principle of art for its own sake.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value careful attention to particulars and the ability to convey them with delicacy; in criticism, look for faithful transmission of a work's charm rather than grand theoretical overreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledging production conditions and fragmentary nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is produced 'under conditions' and what survives may be 'Disjecta membra'—scattered pieces that only intermittently reveal the full utterance of the man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take into account historical, institutional, and practical constraints (e.g., theatre demands) when judging completeness or apparent unevenness; great moments may outshine surrounding conventional matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophetic/deep insight without doctrinal preaching
rubrics_metrics.description: The great writer may be a 'Prophet' in insight—revealing deep 'harmonies with the infinite structure of the Universe'—yet not preach dogma; Shakespeare 'sang; did not preach, except musically.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work attains profound insight while remaining artistic rather than doctrinal; praise that elucidates human experience without proselytising is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: National voice and cultural cohesion value
rubrics_metrics.description: A nation's production of an articulate creative voice (e.g., Shakespeare, Dante) gives it lasting unity and international standing; such figures can rally a dispersed people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When considering cultural importance, factor how a work or author functions as an emblem or cohesive voice for a people or language; assess civic and cultural resonance beyond narrowly aesthetic metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good craftsmanship can be obscured by perfect ease
rubrics_metrics.description: The perfection of a work may 'hide the builder's merit'—the art so fits that the effort appears natural; 'the very perfection of the house... hides the builder's merit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluation, probe beneath apparent effortless mastery to recognize skill and design; the absence of visible artifice can be a sign of superior workmanship, not absence of craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinterestedness / art for its own sake as enduring quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Works produced from 'disinterested' devotion to literature (art for art's sake) often have exceptional endurance—examples: Lamb compared to more polemical contemporaries whose topicality fades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value disinterested, non-utilitarian artistic aims that focus on beauty and concrete experience; be cautious about overvaluing works tied mainly to transient political or doctrinal campaigns.
